label: early original-phase token (pos 1-4) from {m,k,3,j,h,1,o,2} after a prefix containing b/m/p/q/u
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase, almost entirely at positions 2-3 (about 90% of mass), with some at 1 and 4. It never fires at t=0, at t>=6, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. It prefers current inputs m and k (each about 6x lift), then 3, j, h, 1, o, 2, and it mostly fires on the first occurrence of the token. Magnitude grows when the preceding tokens come from {b, m, p, q, u}. The strongest activations are prefixes like "b b k", "b b m" and "b m k". The behaviour looks like a graded conjunction of token identities in a short early prefix, so the predicate gets about 0.83 of the mass but its precision is low (about 0.27). Requiring both of the two previous tokens to be in the preferred set gives precision 0.57 but loses mass (0.54).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: m, k, 3, j, h, 1; least: i, n, s, r) and the previous input (most: b, m, p, q, 3, u; least: n, f, x, r); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, t=4.
